units.translation: and 818 λειχὴν ἄφυλλος άτεκνος, ἰὼ δίκα [a leafless, childless lichen, oh Justice], the opinion of Heimsoeth is more probable, who, restoring the trimeter, wrote ὦ δίκα δίκα [oh Justice, Justice].
By a more obvious error at the beginning of the trimeter ἰὼ Ζeῦ [oh Zeus] is written in M, where w restored Victorius.
Outside the meter before a dochmius
where it is more probable that it is doubled ἰ ἰώ [oh oh].
unless it should be doubled, as elsewhere before anapaests in the places to be indicated below.

the second syllable of the first ἰώ [oh] being shortened before a vowel in a dochmius, as Sept. 86 ἰὼ ἰὼ θεοί [oh, oh, gods], as is correctly in the apograph instead of the triple iú, which M provides.
where in the antistrophe 1010 and 1011 other words of the same measure correspond.
I deleted what is in Madditum, ἐέ, ἐὴ [alas, alas], meaning.
Rare is ἰὼ ἰώ μοι [oh, oh me], which is read Pers. 973 and cannot be changed into ἰώ μοί μοι [oh me, me], since the antistrophic verse is 988 ἴυγγά μοι δῆτ᾽ [a charm for me indeed].
where I added the second iw from the apographs.

where the corrector added the second ἰώ [oh] in M. [But in the next verse I wrote ὅπου τὸ τιμιώτατον [where the most honored] for ἰὼ ὅπου τιμιώτατον [oh where the most honored], unless someone prefers to write ὅπου ἐστὶ τιμιώτατον [where is the most honored].]
which correspond to words similarly formed in the strophe (v. 113), ἰὴ ἰὴ | ἰηλέμοισιν ἐμπρεπή ζῶσα γόοις με τιμῶ [alas, alas, living conspicuous in wailings, honor me with laments].

corruptly M ἴχαρ φρενί τ᾽ ἄταν. ἰὼ ἰὸν | λεῖφ᾽ ἕδρανα cet. [a delight and ruin to the mind. Oh, oh, leave the seats etc.], where it is uncertain whether ἰὼ ἰώ [oh, oh] with Robortello or ἰοὺ ἰού [oh, oh] with Hermann should be written.
Oh all-powerful gods, oh perfect gods and goddesses
May these things prosper, oh champion of my house
unhappy for them the mother who bore
Oh paternal soil of the Argive land
Oh halls of kings, dear roofs
Oh marriages, marriages – oh of Scamander
Oh toils, toils || oh before the towers
Oh all-wretched hearth, oh destructions of houses
Oh gods, you accomplish justly justice
Oh earth, earth, would that you had received me
Oh grievous, unbearable sorrows, oh pain hard to cease
Oh wretched I, of a hateful fate
Alas, alas, oh, oh. Oh, oh divinities
Oh, oh house, house and chiefs
Oh, oh, lord of grievous evils
Oh, oh, where shall we bury them in the earth?
Oh, oh, a grief to the father, a bedfellow
Oh, oh, Persian land, hard to traverse
Oh, oh, oh, hard-to-judge toils. Where will this wave carry me?
oh unhappy for them the mother who bore
a leafless, childless lichen, oh Justice
